data.question: Analyse the relationship between maternal age and delivery complications.

aiDisclosure.note: Statistics are calculated by deterministic code. The AI selects the method and writes the explanation.
aiDisclosure.dataSent: Question text, column names, inferred types, missing percentages, category labels (up to 15 per column) and aggregate statistics. No row-level values and no columns flagged as personal data.
aiDisclosure.rationale: Compares mean maternal age between patients with and without delivery complications.

data.interpretation: Women with delivery complications had a higher mean maternal age of 33.75 compared to 28.644231 for those without complications, a mean difference of -5.105769 years. The result is statistically significant at alpha 0.05 (p = 0.0055), with a 95% confidence interval of [-8.531569, -1.679969] and a large effect size (Cohen's d = -0.814852). Welch's test does not assume equal variances and assumes independent observations, but this analysis describes association only and does not establish causation, as unmeasured confounding may affect the observed relationship.
assumptions: Welch's test is used, so equal variances are not assumed. Observations are assumed independent.
limitations: Results use complete cases only. Rows with a missing value in an analysed variable are excluded.
These statistics describe association in this dataset. They do not establish causation.
Unmeasured confounding can affect every association in observational healthcare data.
